About BikeTourFrance.net
Eat. Sleep. Roll. Repeat.
I'm John—the cyclist behind BikeTourFrance.net. I help riders execute extraordinary bicycle tours in France.

I personally lead four very small, self-supported group tours each year. Groups have fewer than 12 riders, so I can lead the ride, communicate each day's plan in depth, and give the group the attention it needs.

If you prefer to travel on your own schedule, I offer a self-guided tour package. I build the routes, book your accommodations, and provide practical support as you prepare for the trip. You ride independently, with a sound plan and help when you need it.

All BikeTourFrance tours are self-supported. You carry your own gear from place to place. The Canal des Deux Mers is fairly flat, so you do not need to obsess over every gram. But space still matters. Pack less than you think you need.

Planning a bicycle tour in France gets complex fast. Where you ride, how far you go, where you eat, where you sleep, how trains fit in, and when you stop to see a place all affect one another. A small choice early in the plan can cause a hard day later.

I have planned and ridden self-supported tours across France. I have also traveled on foot in many parts of the country. I know what works on the ground: routes that make sense, days that fit real riders, places to stay, food stops, train options, and the small details that keep a trip moving well. I also know that coordinating your arrival time with your lodging can make a big difference for everyone.

Outside of touring, I lead rides for Cascade Bicycle Club in Seattle, work in enterprise technology, and hold DELF B2 certification in French. I'm not a camper—I like a good route, a real bed, a warm shower, and a solid meal at the end of the day. It is France, after all, and I love to eat well.

You arrange your own travel to Bordeaux and home from Sète. Most riders arrange to leave their bike case in Bordeaux at the hotel during the tour and take the SNCF (sncf.com) train back to Bordeaux after leaving Sète. DON'T FORGET TO BOOK A SPOT FOR YOUR BIKE! Since you will be packing your bike in the case before flying home, I suggest you book your last night at the same hotel we stay at the Friday before we roll out. If you decide to take a train to a following town during the tour, that will be your own expense. Tour activities end Monday after dinner.   Tuesday breakfast is included in the tour although there will be no formal meeting that morning.

What is it?
Direct tram connection from Bordeaux Airport (Mérignac) to Gare Saint-Jean (main train station). Launched Dec 6, 2025.
Direct coach shuttle from Bordeaux Airport to Gare Saint-Jean. No intermediate stops, no transfers.
How often does it run?
Every 10 min (Mon–Sat) / Every 15 min (Sun/holidays). First: ~5am. Last: Midnight (Mon–Wed), 1am (Thu–Sat)
Limited: 07:30–20:05 daily. Mon–Fri: ~22 runs. Sat/Sun: ~14 runs. Not available early morning or late evening.
How long does it take?
~45 minutes. Direct, no transfers.
~30 minutes (traffic dependent)
How much does it cost?
€1.90 per ticket
€9 online / €10 on board
What about my bike?

✅ Bikes in cases: Always
✅ Bikes not in cases: 9am–4pm only
❌ NOT 7am–9am or 4pm–7pm
Pack in case to avoid rush hours.
TBM Bicycle Rules: 05 57 57 88 88

✅ Bikes in cases: Yes
✅ Bikes not in cases: Yes
Requirement: Closed bag, labeled with name, phone, address.
Carrier may refuse oversized items.
Bikes not in cases = anytime transport (no restrictions).
30'Direct FAQ: 30direct.com
How do I book?

No booking required. Buy ticket at tram stop (vending machine), TBM mobile app (Bordeaux transit app), or Relay newsstand at airport.

To board: Validate your ticket on the platform or onboard validators (card readers, white validators, or TBM app via Bluetooth). Self-validate and board—no ticket inspection.

Book online at 30direct.com or pay €10 on board. Book in advance for €9 rate.

To board: Show your ticket to the driver (printed, phone e-ticket, or mobile). Tickets can be purchased directly from the driver. Visa/Mastercard accepted onboard (American Express not accepted).

What riders say

“We did the Atlantic France tour with BikeTourFrance in 2024. My main apprehension was navigating and wayfinding in a foreign country—not the distance itself.
